questions.q: In nano, which shortcut saves the current file?
questions.explain: Ctrl+O ('write out') saves the file in nano, prompting you to confirm the filename. Ctrl+X exits, Ctrl+W searches, and Ctrl+K cuts the current line.

questions.q: You open a file in vim and start typing, but nothing appears as text — instead strange things happen on screen. What's the most likely cause?
options: vim is broken and needs to be reinstalled
vim opened in normal mode, where keystrokes are interpreted as commands, not text — insert mode must be entered first
questions.explain: vim starts in normal mode, where every keystroke is a command. You must press i to switch to insert mode before typed characters are inserted into the file as text.

questions.q: In vim's normal mode, what does the command `dd` do?
questions.explain: dd deletes the current line in normal mode (and places it in vim's register, so it can be pasted with p). yy performs the equivalent copy, or 'yank.'

questions.q: What is the difference between `:wq` and `:q!` in vim?
options: They do the same thing; `:q!` is just a faster shortcut
`:wq` saves and quits; `:q!` quits without saving, forcing past the unsaved-changes warning
`:wq` only works in insert mode; `:q!` only works in normal mode
questions.explain: `:wq` writes (saves) the file before quitting. `:q!` quits immediately and discards any unsaved changes — the `!` forces the exit past vim's normal refusal to quit with unsaved edits.

questions.q: Why does nano not require you to think about 'modes' the way vim does?
options: nano has no save function, so modes are unnecessary
nano only works on empty files
In nano, whatever you type is inserted directly at the cursor; shortcuts are always accessed via Ctrl combinations rather than a separate command mode
nano actually has the same modal system as vim, just hidden
questions.explain: nano behaves like a simple text box: typed characters are always inserted as text, and all commands are triggered with Ctrl key combinations rather than a mode switch. vim instead toggles between normal mode (commands) and insert mode (text).
